articles.body: amage the pins or lift the solder pads further, which turns a simple port replacement into a bigger board repair. Stop using it and leave it unplugged. Can an HDMI port be repaired? Usually, You switch on your PS5 and the screen stays black, even though the console's lights and fans say it's running. Before you buy a new TV or cable, it's worth knowing that the HDMI port itself is one of the most common points of failure on modern consoles. Here's how to tell what's going on. Why HDMI ports fail The HDMI socket is soldered to the motherboard, and it takes a lot of physical stress. Cables get tugged, consoles get knocked, and plugging and unplugging over the years loosens the metal pins and the solder joints holding them. Once the port is damaged, no cable will fix it.

articles.title: Alpenglow: How Solana Swaps Its Consensus in One Slot
articles.excerpt: Solana consensus has been using the same design since 2020. Every validator publishes votes as transactions in the blocks, adds increasingly strong lockouts and declares a block final once 32 more blo…
articles.body: Solana consensus has been using the same design since 2020. Every validator publishes votes as transactions in the blocks, adds increasingly strong lockouts and declares a block final once 32 more blocks have built upon it. It works, but it lacks a published safety proof, consumes over half of all transactions in the network, and its finality takes seconds despite the rest of the stack working in milliseconds. Alpenglow is its replacement. The design is due to Quentin Kniep, Jakub Sliwinski, and Roger Wattenhofer, who left ETH Zurich and joined Anza after publishing their research on liveness issues in TowerBFT. Alpenglow was published in May 2025.

articles.title: I benchmarked 8 PDF extractors on 27 documents from 1 to 487 pages. Here's what broke, and what won.
articles.excerpt: I knew something was off when two numbers landed in the same afternoon. Every tool that reads the PDF text layer had scored exactly 0.00 on every chart in my corpus. Fine, I thought, the charts are im…
articles.body: I knew something was off when two numbers landed in the same afternoon. Every tool that reads the PDF text layer had scored exactly 0.00 on every chart in my corpus. Fine, I thought, the charts are images, there's nothing in the text layer to read. Then PyMuPDF came in at a perfect 1.00 on clean text. Every document. Every page-count bucket. Not 0.98. 1.00. The first number was telling me something true about the tools. The second was telling me something true about me. PyMuPDF got 1.00 because the "ground truth" for clean-text documents was PyMuPDF's own output. I'd written the answer key with one of the contestants and hadn't noticed. A reviewer did. So this is partly a benchmark write-up and partly a list of the ways a benchmark can quietly lie to the person who built it.

articles.body: Introduction Building a website involves more than making content appear in a browser. A good website should have a clear structure, communicate meaning through its HTML, and be accessible to different users. While building my personal portfolio, I explored semantic HTML and performed an accessibility audit to understand how these principles improve web development. What Is Semantic HTML? Semantic HTML uses elements that describe the purpose of their content. For example, " " identifies introductory content, "" represents navigation, "" identifies the primary content, and "" represents footer information. Using generic " " elements for every section may produce a visible webpage, but it doesn't communicate the same meaning to browsers, developers, and assistive technologies.

articles.title: It's time to reassess the size of our solar system, scientists say
articles.excerpt: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system based on the Milky Way's gravity, including its dark matter.
articles.body: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system by presenting a theory which states that measurements of the Milky Way's gravitational field, including its dark matter, redraws the sun's frontier. That theory was put forward by Jim Green, former NASA chief scientist and past director of the space agency's Planetary Science Division, along with Ed Belbruno, a professor of mathematics at Yeshiva University and a senior research associate at Princeton University. The solar system's gravitational frontier extends to nearly 3.8 light-years from the sun , they contend, roughly 241,000 astronomical units (AU), a distance that brings the "edge" of the solar system to within the same scale as the separation between neighboring stars.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.
